newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE CONFIDENCE GROWING FOR SECOND TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ZIMBABWE CONFIDENCE GROWING FOR SECOND TEST.

text.p: Zimbabwe confidence is mounting ahead of the second test against England starting on Thursday despite touring team coach David Lloyd's claim his side "flippin' murdered them" in the drawn first test.
The inaugural test between the two teams ended in Bulawayo on Sunday in a draw with the scores level -- the first time there has been such a result in test cricket history.

England led by only 30 on first innings and struggled to polish off Zimbabwe's second innings on the final day, but Lloyd repeatedly said after the match: "We flippin' murdered them and they know it."
In contrast, Zimbabwe captain Alistair Campbell said: "I thought we held our own and at times dominated, especially on the first two days."
Campbell said they were confident going into the opening game of the two-test encounter and "we'll be even more so in Harare".
The Harare Sports Club was the venue of Zimbabwe's only test win, against Pakistan in February last year, since they became a test-playing country four years ago.

In that Zimbabwe victory by an innings and 64 runs, Grant Flower made a double century, Andy Flower and Guy Whittall both scored hundreds and paceman Heath Streak had a nine-wicket match haul. All four are to face England.

Zimbabwe are likely to make one change from Bulawayo, with batsman Stuart Carlisle being dropped in favour of Mark Dekker, the left-hander who hit a century for Matabeleland in the four-day game against England which preceded the first test.

England can reflect on some plus points from the first test, with centuries by Nasser Hussain and John Crawley and runs in both innings for opener Nick Knight and Alec Stewart, whose 73 from 75 deliveries on the last day initially fired England's victory hopes as they chased 205 in 37 overs.

Off-spinner Robert Croft bowled well in the first innings and left-arm spinner Phil Tufnell was effective in the second. Paceman Chris Silverwood, though ignored by Mike Atherton for most of the second innings, had a creditable test debut.
However, England's new ball attack of Darren Gough and Alan Mullally was never threatening and a familiar inability to clean up the tail let Zimbabwe off the hook in both innings.
The long England tail was exposed in the first innings and for lengthy periods on the first three days the touring side were saving the game, not winning it.
England will have to decide whether to include the recently-arrived Craig White, who has been added to the tour party as cover for fellow all-rounder Ronnie Irani, ruled out by back trouble.
On his performance in Bulawayo, Mullally should be the one to make way, with Silverwood being given the new ball, but England's management will probably decide against such a radical move.
The Harare Sports Club pitch is likely to be as batsman friendly as the one in Bulawayo and the smart money will be on a draw.
